statement: Whenever find_distance(root, p, q) returns a result r, r equals the distance between the node of value p and the node of value q, defined as the least k >= 0 for which there exist values v_0, ..., v_k with v_0 = p, v_k = q, and for every i with 0 <= i < k the nodes of value v_i and v_{i+1} are joined by a parent-child edge in root (one is the parent of the other).
preconditions: root is a binary tree in which p and q each occur as the value of some node (i.e., there is a node of root with value p and a node of root with value q), and all node values of root are distinct.

statement: find_distance(root, p, q) returns a result r (it does not fail).
preconditions: root has between 1 and 10^4 nodes, every node value is in the range [0, 10^9], all node values of root are distinct, and p and q each occur as the value of some node of root.

statement: Whenever find_distance(root, p, q) returns a result r, r <= N(root) - 1, where N(root) is the number of nodes of root.
preconditions: root is a binary tree in which p and q each occur as the value of some node, and all node values of root are distinct.

statement: Whenever find_distance(root, p, q) returns a result r, r <= depth(root, p) + depth(root, q), where depth(T, v) is the number of edges on the unique path from the root of T down to the node of value v.
preconditions: root is a binary tree in which p and q each occur as the value of some node, and all node values of root are distinct.

statement: Whenever find_distance(root, p, q) returns a result r, r >= |depth(root, p) - depth(root, q)|, where depth(T, v) is the number of edges on the unique path from the root of T down to the node of value v.
preconditions: root is a binary tree in which p and q each occur as the value of some node, and all node values of root are distinct.

statement: If the node of value p is the parent of the node of value q, or the node of value q is the parent of the node of value p, then whenever find_distance(root, p, q) returns a result r, r = 1.
preconditions: root is a binary tree in which p and q each occur as the value of some node, and all node values of root are distinct.

statement: Whenever find_distance(root, p, q) returns a result r1 and find_distance(root, q, p) returns a result r2, r1 = r2.
preconditions: root is a binary tree in which p and q each occur as the value of some node, and all node values of root are distinct.

statement: If p != q and the node of value p is an ancestor of the node of value q (that is, it lies on the path from the root down to the node of value q), then whenever find_distance(root, p, q) returns a result r, r = depth(root, q) - depth(root, p), where depth(T, v) is the number of edges on the unique path from the root of T down to the node of value v.
preconditions: root is a binary tree in which p and q each occur as the value of some node, and all node values of root are distinct.

statement: If root is a node with value a, left subtree L and right subtree R, and p occurs in L while q occurs in R (or p occurs in R while q occurs in L), then whenever find_distance(root, p, q) returns a result r, r = depth(root, p) + depth(root, q), where depth(T, v) is the number of edges on the unique path from the root of T down to the node of value v.
preconditions: root is a binary tree in which p and q each occur as the value of some node, and all node values of root are distinct.

statement: If root is a node with value a, left subtree L and right subtree R, and both p and q occur in L, then whenever find_distance(root, p, q) returns a result r1 and find_distance(L, p, q) returns a result r2, r1 = r2.
preconditions: root is a binary tree in which p and q each occur as the value of some node, and all node values of root are distinct.

statement: Whenever find_distance(root, p, q) returns a result r, there exist values v_0, ..., v_r with v_0 = p, v_r = q, and for every i with 0 <= i < r the nodes of value v_i and v_{i+1} are joined by a parent-child edge in root.
preconditions: root is a binary tree in which p and q each occur as the value of some node, and all node values of root are distinct.

statement: Whenever find_distance(root, p, q) returns a result r, if x is the lowest common ancestor of the nodes of value p and q (the unique node of maximum depth that is an ancestor of both), then r = depth(root, p) + depth(root, q) - 2 * depth(root, x), where depth(T, v) is the number of edges on the unique path from the root of T down to the node of value v.
preconditions: root is a binary tree in which p and q each occur as the value of some node, and all node values of root are distinct.
